text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner said on Monday the company had sold 479,000 cars in the first nine months of 1996, an increase of 12 percent over the same period of 1995.
Speaking on the eve of a Paris motor show, Werner told a news conference that he believed the company could sell "well in excess" of 600,000 cars during the full year 1996.
He said nine-month car sales were up 14 percent in western Europe, 19 percent in the United States and 45 percent in Japan.
He said 225,000 E-class cars had left the production line since the beginning of year and added that the commercial vehicle sector had produced a sales increase of eight percent in September.
